findings.finding: Repeated canonical encoding and hashing is not the cost of a participant that caches the fixed SHA-256 prefix. Measured valid optimized work is faster on both owned hosts. The old 60-second reference calculation cannot serve as an adversarial cost budget.
findings.required_resolution: Declare and measure the optimized reference workload, then justify immutable targets and confirmation floor against an explicit attacker/concentration/resource budget. Do not only multiply the old numbers by this observed speedup.

findings.finding: Target ordering, U256 work arithmetic, 32/128 confirmation counts and the 512-header count bound pass. Those arithmetic checks do not prove network availability, GPU/ASIC cost, reorganization probability, flood capacity or independent ownership.
findings.required_resolution: Retain deployment-specific analysis and independent review of those assumptions. The delayed retarget follows four completed contribution-Epoch counts, not wall-clock 60-second block timing.

timing_limits: Expected seconds are arithmetic projections from hash rates, not timed mining or transfer latency.
Single thread, shared hosts, rotating mode order; no maximal optimization or specialized hardware claim.
The cumulative-work floor and minimum successor count do not establish an economic attack cost by themselves.
